messages:
mira (prodops): heads up — I'm starting a quick pass on our internal incident comms templates. want a compact set of canonical sections + tone notes we can ship to eng/oncall and support.
incident-bot: Incident thread created by mira at 2026-03-15T10:12:24Z. Paging: eng-oncall, support-lead. Severity: S2 (customer impact).
alex (eng-oncall): +1. can we please include a short 'what we know / what we're doing / customer impact' framing? that's the thing folks actually copy into status pages.
samir (incident-comm): yes — i drafted a lightweight toolkit earlier this quarter. happy to fold into a single doc. goal: single source of truth for status copy, customer-notify, and internal summary.
cheng (support-lead): priorities: clear customer-facing CTA (e.g., "contact support if you see XYZ") and an ETA field even if speculative. customers want to know next check-in time.
tayla (docs): i can own the markdown but need precise placeholders. propose these canonical placeholders: [INCIDENT_ID], [SEVERITY], [AFFECTED_SERVICES], [START_TIME], [ETA_CHECKIN], [MITIGATION_STATE], [WORKAROUND], [ROOT_CAUSE_TBD].
mira (prodops): nice. suggested standard sections for internal comms (short): 1) Summary (1-2 lines) 2) Impact (who/what/how many customers) 3) Mitigation in progress (actions & owners) 4) Next steps + ETA 5) Postmortem owner. keep each section 1-3 bullets max.
alex (eng-oncall): also include quick runbook link and primary execs to ping for high-sev. we should have a default line: "If this escalates to S1, add: paging TL, oncall backup, and CISO oncall".
samir (incident-comm): tone guidelines — internal: direct, action-oriented, include owner for each action. customer-facing: calm, non-technical, admit uncertainty, promise check-in window. examples:

Customer short status (public):
"We are investigating an issue affecting [AFFECTED_SERVICES]. Some customers may experience [IMPACT]. Our team is working on a fix and we will provide an update by [ETA_CHECKIN]."

Customer long status (email/enterprise):
"Hello —
We’re currently investigating an issue impacting [AFFECTED_SERVICES], which may cause [IMPACT]. Our engineers have identified [MITIGATION_STATE or WORKAROUND if available]. We will follow up by [ETA_CHECKIN] with next steps. If you need immediate assistance, contact your account team or support@redwood.ai."

Internal status (slack):
"[INCIDENT_ID] — Summary: [one-line]. Impact: [bullet]. Owner: [name]. Mitigation: [bullet actions]. ETA next update: [ETA_CHECKIN]."

Please keep templates short; ops copies them into status pages and customer emails frequently.
cheng (support-lead): for enterprise notices, add a "Suggested escalation wording" so AMs know when to loop Legal/Compliance.
tayla (docs): i'll add a short template for 'post-update followup' too — e.g., final update that includes RCA ETA and customer remediation steps.
incident-bot: Reminder: oncall handoff scheduled in 40 minutes. Current owner: alex. Next oncall: samir.
alex (eng-oncall): handoff note: if we're still in mitigation at handoff, include this brief snippet at top of the handoff message: "Handoff: mitigation in progress. Current blockers: [list]. Next steps for incoming oncall: [list]." also include any open Jira/incident tasks.
samir (incident-comm): can we standardize a 'minimal status' for paging messages? something one line for the pager that maps to a public sentence. e.g., "Pager: svc X experiencing errors — mitigation underway — public status: 'Investigating'". keeps consistency between pager and public status.
mira (prodops): yes. also recommend we add 'confidence' field to internal updates (low/medium/high) so exec comms know how sure we are about root cause early on.
cheng (support-lead): +1. also request we include 'known workarounds' early — support will push those to customers to reduce noise.
alex (eng-oncall): technical snippet for runbooks in templates:
```
Runbook: link
Primary action: restart job X (owner: @cheng)
Fallback: route traffic to region fallback
```

keep it small so people copy/paste.
samir (incident-comm): final ask: can we create a short 'cheat sheet' for AMs with suggested subject lines for emails (e.g., "Incident [INCIDENT_ID] — service degraded — update at [ETA]") and a fill-in-the-blank body. i'll prototype and share.
tayla (docs): i'll assemble all pieces into a single markdown in /docs/incidents/voice-toolkit.md and include a tiny changelog for phrasing updates.
mira (prodops): timeline: samir to draft templates today; tayla to assemble tomorrow; we'll do a quick review in incident guild on Thu. if no objections, we ship as 'official wording' for next oncall rotation.
samir (incident-comm): drafted. attaching quick copy below for review (paste-ready):

---
Internal brief (copy for slack):
[INCIDENT_ID] | Severity: [SEVERITY]
Summary: [one-line summary]
Impact: [who/how many]
Mitigation: [actions + owners]
ETA next update: [ETA_CHECKIN]
Confidence: [low/med/high]

Public (status page):
We are aware of an issue affecting [AFFECTED_SERVICES]. We are investigating and will provide an update by [ETA_CHECKIN].

Public (email):
Subject: Incident [INCIDENT_ID] — [AFFECTED_SERVICE] degraded
Body: Hello — We’re investigating reports of [IMPACT] affecting [AFFECTED_SERVICES]. Our engineers are working to restore service. We will update you by [ETA_CHECKIN]. If you need immediate help, contact support@redwood.ai.

Customer follow-up (final):
Subject: Incident [INCIDENT_ID] — resolution and next steps
Body: Hello — The incident affecting [AFFECTED_SERVICES] has been resolved at [RESOLVE_TIME]. Root cause: [ROOT_CAUSE_TBD]. Impact: [summary of customer-facing impact]. Remediation steps: [if any]. If you require more detail, contact your account team.
---

alex (eng-oncall): LGTM. small nit: add an optional 'workaround' line in public email. that's often helpful.
cheng (support-lead): approved from support side. please include AM escalation triggers (time thresholds) in the toolkit.
mira (prodops): perfect. samir — when you post the PR please include a sample filled example with placeholders replaced so people see how it looks. we'll promote in the next oncall rotation onboarding.
samir (incident-comm): will do. thanks all :)
